lines: {target}? Strange quiet can make a place feel too safe. I would mark the way home first.
If anyone heads for Mushroom Fields, tell them: Eat only what you know and keep your boat close. I will be at the map table.
Mycelium underfoot is not village dirt. I'll mark that beside the road home.
Mushroom Fields is no small story. A map is not courage.
I will remember Mushroom Fields as odd land where even the grass changed its mind. I will mark the warning beside the road.
{target}? I would not rush toward it without telling someone where you are going first.
That kind of place makes a simple walk feel like a decision. Pack food, count your torches, and keep your head clear.
I have heard enough about {target} to know the quiet parts are usually the ones to worry about.
If you go there, come back with the story and not just the scratches. The village remembers both.
A place like {target} can turn confidence into <shake>panic</shake> very quickly.
